A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on conformal prediction, distribution shifts, temperature scaling, and few-shot adaptation.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations of more models and histogram-binning calibration.

M1.justification: The frozen-backbone linear probing procedure, cross-entropy objective, and LAC/APS/RAPS scoring procedures are retained. Additional pretrained models and histogram binning extend the evaluated comparisons rather than introduce a proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet and its four shifted variants, and the same ten additional few-shot classification datasets. Four-shot results already appear in v2's appendix. The changed allocation of data to training concerns protocol within retained coverage.

E2.justification: The general and calibration comparisons expand from 11 to 17 models, adding Phi 3.5, LLaVa, CLIP ViT-L, ViT-H, ConvNeXt, and ConvNeXt-L. Histogram binning becomes an evaluated calibration alternative. The three CP methods and the ZS, ZSLP, CLAP, CoOp, and KgCoOp few-shot comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Section 4.2.2 changes the stated adaptation data from each target ImageNet variant to ImageNet. However, the following test description remains inconsistent and the reported shift means are retained, so this establishes a reported protocol revision, not a rerun. The new histogram-binning experiment uses 100 bins and separate fitting/testing sets. Appendix performance columns also change from accuracy to F1 without explaining the relationship.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a calibration robustness investigation beyond temperature scaling, testing histogram binning across 17 models. Figure 2 and the appendix temperature sweeps also extend the worst-class and sensitivity analyses to six additional models. Existing distribution-shift analyses remain, with several plots merely regrouped.

E5.justification: v3 adds systematic ± reporting to general-setting, distribution-shift, and few-shot tables that previously contained point estimates. Neither version specifies corresponding run counts, and v3 does not explain whether these quantities are standard deviations, standard errors, or intervals. Additional runs therefore cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: v3 adds results for six models, histogram binning, and marginal coverage in Table 1. Numerous entries labeled MCCC are replaced: DINO-S/APS on CIFAR-10 changes from 0.010 to 0.930 in Table 5, indicating corrected reporting rather than a demonstrated performance gain. New Table 9 reports CLIP/APS set size increasing from 9.50 to 337.35 under histogram binning, with MCCC decreasing from 0.556 to 0.374.

T1.justification: Section 4.2.1 corrects class-conditional coverage from P(Y=y | Y in S(X)) to P(Y in S(X) | Y=y). The remaining CP definitions and reasoning are retained; moving metric formulas into the main text does not introduce new theory.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its general claim that transformer models conformalize better than CNNs to smaller conformal-metric degradation under domain shift. The principal abstract claims about foundation models, calibration, APS, and few-shot adaptation remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds an accuracy-based justification for selecting the supervised-versus-foundation-model comparisons and application-dependent guidance about coverage versus set size. It also softens anticipating optimal APS coverage gap from calibration into an observed association, and discusses the different MCCC behavior under histogram binning.

D1.justification: New Table 4 documents parameter counts, training schemes, modalities, and architectures. Appendix C.2 supplies the histogram-binning setting and fitting/testing separation. Existing optimizer, learning rate, RAPS hyperparameters, and target coverage levels are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Phi-3 technical report by Abdin et al. and Visual Instruction Tuning by Liu et al. for the added model families. The related-work discussion and overall research positioning otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes local wording and terminology edits, updates author information, moves metric definitions into Section 4.1, and reorganizes the calibration appendix with subsections. Most paragraphs and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation, extensively resizing and relocating displays. Tables gain columns and uncertainty entries, new model-summary and histogram-binning tables appear, and existing appendix figures are merged. Figure 1 also develops dataset/scale inconsistencies relative to its caption and Tables 5–7.

improvement.justification: The broader model/calibration comparisons and corrected coverage definition and tables are useful gains. However, v3 introduces a Figure 1 mismatch with the named datasets' table values and an internally inconsistent revision of the distribution-shift protocol while retaining its results. The added ± quantities are unexplained. These benefits and reporting problems prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
